ἀγρεύει. Καὶ ἡ 13.32 ἀγρευομένη ὑπὸ γυναικὸς ψυχὴ τιμία ἐστὶ τῇ φύ σει· οὐ γάρ ἐστι
τῇ φύσει χοϊκή. Ἢ ἐπειδὴ τῶν ἀν δρείων τὸ φρόνημα καὶ ἡ ψυχὴ τιμία, ὅμως καὶ ταύ
τας ἀγρεύει. {1ΚΕΦ. Ηʹ.}1 Ἐγὼ ἤμην ᾗ προσέχαιρε. Τὸ, ἤμην, ἐπὶ Θεοῦ χρόνον οὐ
προσημαίνει· χρονικὸν γὰρ, ἡνίκα τι τῶν ὑπὸ χρόνον προσημαίνει, ὡς τὸ, Ἤμην ἐν
ἀγορᾷ. Εἰ δὲ παρὰ Θεῷ ἦν ἁρμόζουσα τῷ ἀνάρχῳ, ἀΐδιος καὶ αὐτή. {1ΚΕΦ. Ιʹ.}1 Αὕτη
πλουτίζει. Εἰ πᾶς ὁ εὐλογημένος παρὰ Κυρίου πλούσιος, οἱ δὲ πορευόμενοι ἐν νόμῳ
Κυρίου εὐλογοῦνται ὑπὸ Κυρίου, ἐπορεύθησαν δὲ ἐν νόμῳ Κυρίου προφῆται· οὗτοι
ἄρα πλούσιοι ἦσαν. Ἐν γέλωτι ἄφρων πράσσει κακά. Πράττων τὰ κακὰ ἥδεται καὶ
χαίρει. Ἡ δὲ σοφία ἀνδρὶ τίκτει φρόνησιν, πρακτικὴν ἀρετήν. {1ΚΕΦ. ΙΑʹ.}1 Ὁ μὴ
συμπεριφερόμενος τῷ ἑαυτοῦ οἴκῳ, κλη ρονομήσει ἀνέμους. Οἶκος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν
ἐστιν ἐν ᾧ κινούμεθα καὶ ἐσμέν. Ὁ ἐν ταῖς ἐντολαῖς οὖν τοῦ Θεοῦ μὴ περιπατῶν
συγκληρονόμος ἔσται τῶν ἐναν τίων
pass_a_gloss: The catch continues: she snares. And the soul that a woman has snared is precious in its nature, because by nature it is not of the dust. Or, since the thinking and the soul belonging to the courageous are precious, she nevertheless snares even those. Under chapter eight: I was the one in whom he took delight. When I-was is said about God it does not point ahead to time; the form is temporal only when it marks something placed under time, as when someone says I was in the market. But if she was beside God in a manner suited to the One without beginning, then she herself is everlasting too. Under chapter ten: This one makes rich. If every person blessed from the Lord is rich, and those who walk in the Lord’s law are blessed from the Lord, and the prophets walked in the Lord’s law, those prophets therefore were rich. In laughter a fool works evils: while working the evils he is pleased and rejoices. Wisdom, however, gives birth to prudence for a man — virtue that is put into practice. Under chapter eleven: The one who does not move about with his own house will inherit winds. House for us is God, in whom we are moved and we are. So the one who does not walk about in the commandments of God will be fellow heir with the powers set against us. Out of fruit of righteousness a tree of life is grown. Fruit of righteousness means the end-point of virtue. Anyone has as many trees of life as he has fruits of righteousness. This tree of life is the one planted in paradise’s middle, which Adam is kept from touching after the sin, once he has thrown away the seeds of righteousness from which the tree of life is grown. pass_b_english: She hunts. And the soul hunted by a woman is precious by nature, for it is not earthy by nature. Or again: since the mindset and soul of the brave are precious, she still hunts even these.

Chapter 8: “I was the one in whom he rejoiced.” Said of God, “I was” does not mark time. It is temporal when it points to something under time, as in “I was in the marketplace.” But if she was with God in a way that fits the One without beginning, she herself is everlasting.

Chapter 10: “She enriches.” If everyone the Lord blesses is rich, and those who walk in the Lord’s law are blessed by the Lord, and the prophets walked in the Lord’s law, then those prophets were rich. “In laughter a fool does evil”: while he does evil he takes pleasure and rejoices. Wisdom, by contrast, bears understanding for a man—practical virtue.

Chapter 11: “Whoever does not go about with his own house will inherit winds.” Our house is God, in whom we move and are. So the one who does not walk in God’s commandments will share inheritance with the opposing powers. “From the fruit of righteousness a tree of life grows.” The fruit of righteousness is virtue’s end. A person has as many trees of life as fruits of righteousness. This is the tree of life planted in the middle of paradise, which Adam is barred from touching after the sin, having thrown away the seeds of righteousness from which that tree grows.
